headline: TSMC, the maker of Nvidia's chips, reports its quarterly results on 15 October, which The Motley Fool's Daniel Sparks calls the best early read on demand behind Nvidia's next quarter.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: read in full, but it is one columnist's preview of an event still to come, with the stock-valuation passages left out.
importance_line: What changed is that TSMC's report on 15 Oct will give an early read on AI chip demand, which matters first to savers whose funds hold chip shares, then to AI companies short of chips, then to Nvidia and TSMC, and the doubt is that TSMC's figures mix Nvidia with other customers and cannot show what Nvidia charges.
summary: The Motley Fool's Daniel Sparks writes that TSMC, which manufactures Nvidia's AI chips, reports its July-to-September results on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, having guided for revenue of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion, about 37% above a year earlier at the midpoint. He says the report includes rivals' chips as well as Nvidia's, so it cannot show what Nvidia charges, and points to two things to watch: growth in TSMC's high-performance computing business and its advanced-packaging capacity, which TSMC's chief executive said in July is so tight that it limits customers' growth.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text of the Yahoo Finance page, which republishes the Motley Fool article, so The Motley Fool is the source and the link is the Yahoo page where it was read. The text's stock-valuation and stock-pick passages are left out (no buy or sell advice).
